items.title: Closed top-level shape and minimum routing identity are explicit
items.statement: The schema explicitly closes the top-level object, fixes both schema_id and artifact_type, requires core project/run/attempt identity, requires at least one non-empty routing_ref, and requires a non-empty type_payload. These are concrete structural guarantees rather than inferred behavior.

items.title: Restore integrity and lifecycle state are structurally unauditable
items.statement: The required freshness, health, retention, and creation-time fields are unconstrained strings, while type_payload is only a non-empty object. No completeness flag, content digest, restore-readiness state, version/generation, idempotency key, ordering rule, atomicity marker, partial-write state, network-availability state, rollback target, or destructive-restore safeguard is defined. A syntactically valid artifact can therefore represent stale, racing, partial, corrupt, offline-unavailable, non-rollbackable, or unsafe restore data without being rejected.
items.impact: Consumers cannot safely decide whether a restore point is complete, current, mutually consistent, recoverable, or safe to apply, and concurrent or interrupted production can silently publish unusable restore points.

items.title: Authority, privacy, provenance, and reference boundaries are opaque
items.statement: Actor, producer, provider-attempt, usage-event, receipt, detail, content, and routing references are optional or minimally constrained strings with no namespace, tenant, ownership, authorization, URI/path safety, referential-integrity, or trust-domain rule. Retention has no expiry, deletion, legal-hold, redaction, or sensitivity semantics, and observability lacks a required producer/actor, trace or correlation identity, immutable receipt chain, and failure provenance. Untrusted or cross-tenant references can pass structural validation and cross-document consumers cannot prove what authority or lifecycle applies.
items.impact: Restore metadata or content may be disclosed, routed, retained, or acted on across the wrong authority boundary, while support tooling cannot establish a complete provenance chain.

items.title: Consumer, presentation, scale, migration, and semantic test contracts are absent
items.statement: The schema names no required callers or consumers and defines no restore command/result seam. Arbitrary freshness/health strings and an unconstrained summary can drive misleading GUI states; no stable status vocabulary, reason code, user-safe/localizable message key, locale, accessible presentation semantics, or timestamp format exists. Arrays and payloads have no maximum sizes or uniqueness rules. The v1 envelope has no payload discriminator/version or migration compatibility rule. Consequently only shallow shape tests are falsifiable; semantic tests for restorable content, GUI truth, accessibility, localization, scale, consumer propagation, and forward/backward compatibility have no oracle, leaving unknown payload-specific hazards unbounded.
items.impact: Different consumers can interpret the same valid artifact incompatibly, UI and support surfaces can overstate restore safety, large artifacts can exhaust resources, and migrations cannot be validated reliably.

dimension_assessments.summary: No caller, consumer, restore-command, or result-propagation contract is named.
Freshness, health, retention, time, and payload admit semantically invalid states with no transition vocabulary.
No generation, compare-and-swap token, idempotency identity, or ordering rule protects concurrent production or use.
No completeness, atomicity, checksum, or partial-write marker distinguishes a complete restore point from an interrupted one.
Restore readiness, rollback target, verification, and post-failure recovery semantics are absent.
Opaque optional actor and producer references do not establish tenant, ownership, or authorization boundaries.
Retention is an arbitrary string and there are no sensitivity, expiry, deletion, redaction, or legal-hold rules for referenced content.
Reference strings and type_payload have no path, URI, namespace, trust-domain, or payload-shape constraints.
Arbitrary freshness, health, summary, and timestamp values can be rendered as trustworthy despite lacking validated meaning.
No local availability, materialization, synchronization, retry, or network-loss state is represented.
Reference arrays, summary text, and type_payload have no upper bounds; arrays also lack uniqueness constraints.
Potentially user-visible summary and status semantics provide no accessible presentation contract or stable machine-readable reason vocabulary.
No locale, localized-message key, structured parameters, or normative date-time format is defined.
The fixed v1 envelope provides no type_payload version, discriminator, capability negotiation, or migration rule.
Producer, actor, receipts, and usage references are optional and no trace, correlation, failure, or immutable provenance chain is required.
No restore target, overwrite scope, dry-run, confirmation, authorization, or rollback safeguard is represented.
Identifiers and refs lack namespaces and referential-integrity rules, leaving external producer and consumer seams ambiguous.
Structural validation is testable, but semantic validity, restoration success, consumer propagation, and UI truth lack acceptance oracles.
The unconstrained type_payload and opaque reference ecosystem leave payload-specific hazards and consumer assumptions intentionally unbounded.
